items.stem: A card is drawn from a deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king given that it is a face card?

In a random experiment, the probability of event A is 0.3 and the probability of event B is 0.5. The probability that both A and B occur is 0.15. What is the probability that at least one of A or B occurs?
A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads if it is known that the first toss is a head?
What is the formula for conditional probability P(E|F)?
In Example 4, what is the value of P(E ∩ F)?
A die is thrown twice. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7, given that the first die shows a number greater than 4?
Which of the following is the multiplication rule of probability for two events E and F?
What is the definition of independent events in probability?
What is the condition for two events A and B to be independent?
In a single toss of a fair coin, what is the probability of getting a head?
What is the definition of a partition of a sample space according to the passage?

A test for a disease is 90% accurate for those who have the disease and 99% accurate for those who do not. If 0.1% of the population has the disease, and a person tests positive, what is the probability that they actually have the disease?
In the experiment of tossing three coins, what is the probability of the event 'at least two heads'?
What is the term used for a real-valued function whose domain is the sample space of a random experiment?

A machine produces 90% acceptable items when correctly set up and 40% acceptable items when incorrectly set up. 80% of setups are correct. After a setup, two acceptable items are produced. What is the probability that the machine was correctly set up?

A patient has a 40% chance of having a heart attack. A meditation and yoga course reduces the risk by 30%, and a drug reduces it by 25%. A patient chooses one of the two options with equal probability. It is given that the patient suffers a heart attack. What is the probability that the patient followed the meditation and yoga course?
If P(A | B) > P(A), which of the following must be true?

A patient has a 40% chance of having a heart attack. A meditation and yoga course reduces the risk by 30% and a drug reduces the risk by 25%. The patient chooses either option with equal probability. If the patient suffers a heart attack, what is the probability that they chose the meditation and yoga course?
What is the probability that a person selected at random is actually having HIV given that he/she is tested HIV+ive, according to the passage?
In a game, a person wins if they get a head on a coin toss. The probability of getting a head is 0.5. What is the probability that a person wins the game in the first or second toss?
What is the probability that a man is speaking the truth when he reports that a die shows a six, according to the passage?
A bolt is drawn at random from the product and is found to be defective. What is the probability that it is manufactured by machine B, according to the passage?
What is the probability that a student chosen at random from the college has an A grade and is a hostlier, according to the passage?
What is the condition for two events A and B to be independent?
What is the formula for calculating the probability of an event A using the theorem of total probability?
What is the condition for a set of events to be a partition of a sample space S?
In a school, 430 students are girls, and 10% of them study in class XII. What is the probability that a randomly chosen student studies in class XII given that the chosen student is a girl?
If A and B are independent events, what is the value of P(A ∩ B)?
If P(A) ≠ 0 and P(B | A) = 1, what is the relationship between A and B?
A box contains 10 cards numbered 1 to 10. One card is drawn at random. What is the probability that the card drawn has an even number, given that the number on the card is more than 3?
A family has two children. What is the probability that both children are boys given that at least one of them is a boy?
In Example 5, what is the probability of event A given that event B has occurred?
In Example 7, what is the conditional probability of the event that the die shows a number greater than 4, given that there is at least one tail?
